work_or_witness: Ultima · Player Quick Reference, p. 5: program-disk instructions and copyright
canonical_term: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar original 1985 Commodore 64 release
original_script: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
definition: The selected original Commodore 64 game/manual witness, whose quick reference instructs players to insert the Ultima IV program disk and identifies ©1985 Origin Systems, Inc.
cultural_caution: A platform/version witness, not a claim that EA's later PC storefront build, ports, reissues, patches, or translations are identical.

citations.locator: Player Quick Reference, p. 5: program-disk instructions and copyright
supports: C64 program-disk context and 1985 Origin Systems copyright

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, pp. 3–4; Ultima · About the game, line 64
definition: The empire/continent the manual says Lord British united and rules, and which EA describes as a world at peace.
cultural_caution: A realm term, not a character, a uniformly peaceful social category, or proof that every historical/manual claim is uncontroversial fact.

supports: Britannia's formation, Lord British's rule, and continent identification

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, p. 37, Lord British afterword
definition: Lord British's search for a new standard and a person who can be a shining example to guide the nation from an Age of Darkness toward an Age of Light.
cultural_caution: A quest/aspirational standard, not a named player character, proof that any seeker succeeds, or a generic moral-classification system.

citations.locator: The History of Britannia, p. 37, Lord British afterword
supports: Quest definition, new standard, shining example, and Age of Darkness/Light language

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, p. 37, Lord British afterword
definition: The desired state in the Quest: the manual says earlier seekers attained enlightenment in one or more of the Eight Virtues, but none had yet attained the true state of being an Avatar.
cultural_caution: A player-seeker role/state rather than a stable named character in this pass; no player name, identity, profession, virtue record, party, or ending is asserted.

citations.locator: The History of Britannia, p. 37, Lord British afterword
supports: Avatar state, previous seekers, and Quest framing

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, pp. 35–37
definition: The eight Virtues in which the manual says prior seekers may become enlightened as part of the Avatar quest.
cultural_caution: Source-native ethical/ritual vocabulary; individual virtues, real-world moral equivalences, and every player/named person's progress are not inferred from this limited witness.

supports: Eight Virtues, paths, enlightenment, and Quest framing

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, p. 10
definition: Companions who aid and fight with the player but can desert if the player strays from their beliefs; the manual distinguishes them from servants or mercenaries.
cultural_caution: A player-dependent party system, not a universal named roster, fixed individual loyalty, or a character-to-character relationship edge.

supports: Free Companions, aid/fight role, belief-dependent desertion, and party-trust wording

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, p. 8
definition: The eight profession framework around which the manual says Britannia's towns have developed cultural centres.
cultural_caution: A role system, not a claim that a particular player or named individual has one fixed profession, or that towns/roles are characters.

supports: Eight towns, cultural centres, and eight major professions

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, p. 15
definition: Sites where each town's devout meditate on their path; each shrine responds to a different Mantra, and the manual links enlightenment to careful consistency and concentration.
cultural_caution: In-setting ritual/system terminology, not a character, real-world religious description, or proof that meditation yields a universal result for every player.

supports: Shrines, Mantra, meditation, and enlightenment wording

work_or_witness: Ultima · The History of Britannia, pp. 15–16
definition: A travel-related phenomenon whose properties are studied under Lord British's auspices to improve understanding of travel across Britannia.
cultural_caution: A setting/travel system, not a character, guaranteed transportation result, or a basis for assigning named-character relationships.

supports: Moon Gates, Lord British's sponsored study, and travel framing
